text:
## Observations

1. The input always has exactly three characters: a digit, `x`, and another digit.
2. Both digits are between 1 and 9 inclusive, so their product is between 1 and 81 inclusive.
3. The output must contain only the integer product.

## Solution sketch

1. “The input always has exactly three characters: a digit, `x`, and another digit.”  
   Read the input line. Take the first and third characters, ignore the middle `x`, and convert each digit to an integer.

2. “Both digits are between 1 and 9 inclusive, so their product is between 1 and 81 inclusive.”  
   Multiply the two integers. The same operation handles all valid inputs, including the smallest product from `1x1` and the largest from `9x9`.

3. “The output must contain only the integer product.”  
   Print the result without any extra text. The algorithm takes O(1) time and O(1) extra space because the input length is fixed.
